rule: RS-15. Each entry is one limit the syllabus states, with the pattern C-11 scans learner-facing text for. The sentence is the syllabus’s; the pattern is our judgement of what teaching past the limit would look like. Every contract in the subject carries every entry.

entries.construct: the PED formula or a PED calculation
entries.pattern: \b(?:PED|price elasticity(?: of demand)?)\s*(?:=|equals\b|is calculated\b|formula\b)|\bformula (?:for|of) (?:PED|price elasticity)|(?:percentage|%) change in (?:the )?quantity demanded\s*(?:÷|/|divided by|over)\b|\bcalculat\w*\s+(?:of\s+)?(?:the |its |a )?(?:PED|price elasticity)

must_catch: PED = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price
Calculate the PED for the product.
The formula for price elasticity is simple.
percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
must_allow: Price elastic demand means customers respond strongly to a price change.
When demand is price inelastic, a price rise increases revenue.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Knowledge of the formula and calculations of PED will not be assessed.

must_catch: Construct an income statement for Kalahari Crafts.
Draw up the income statement for the year.
must_allow: The income statement shows revenue, cost of sales and gross profit.
Accountants prepare the income statement at the end of the year.
Calculate the gross profit from the income statement.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Constructing income statements will not be assessed.

entries.construct: constructing a statement of financial position
entries.pattern: \b(?:construct\w*|draw(?:s|ing)? up|drew up)\s+(?:an?\s+|the\s+|this\s+|your own\s+|its\s+)?(?:simple\s+)?(?:statements? of financial position|balance sheets?)\b

must_catch: Draw up a statement of financial position for the shop.
must_allow: Use the statement of financial position to decide how the business is financed.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Constructing statements of financial position will not be assessed.

must_catch: At an exchange rate of N$18 = US$1, the price rises.
Convert US$200 into Namibian dollars at a rate of 18 to 1.
Calculate the new price after the exchange rate changes.
must_allow: A weaker Namibian dollar makes Namibian exports cheaper abroad.
The exchange rate fell, so imported fuel became more expensive.

entries.syllabus_sentence: Exchange rate calculations will not be assessed.
